{"analysis": "The expected rc ends with `\n\n` (startup empty appends a newline). Let me check: expected rc is `"PS1='PROMPT> '\nPS2='CONT> '\nHISTFILE=/dev/null\n\n"`. So startup default empty should append `\n`? Actually the rc content is fixed three lines then append startup. Expected has trailing `\n\n` meaning startup="" contributes `\n`.

Wait, let me look. Expected rc: `PS1='PROMPT> '\nPS2='CONT> '\nHISTFILE=/dev/null\n\n`. So after HISTFILE=/dev/null there's `\n` then `\n` (startup). So startup default is `\n`? Or the rc template ends with `\n` and startup="" adds nothing, giving `.../dev/null\n` only. But expected has two `\n`.

Actually the contract says "追加 startup字符串(默认空)". Default empty. But expected shows `\n\n`. Hmm. Let me reconsider: maybe rc is `PS1=...\nPS2=...\nHISTFILE=/dev/null\n` + startup + `\n`? With startup="" that gives `.../dev/null\n` + `\n` = `\n\n`. Yes! So there's a trailing newline appended after startup.

So rc = "PS1='PROMPT> '\nPS2='CONT> '\nHISTFILE=/dev/null\n" + startup + "\n".

Let me verify: with startup="", result = `PS1='PROMPT> '\nPS2='CONT> '\nHISTFILE=/dev/null\n` + `\n` = matches expected `.../dev/null\n\n`. Yes.
